failure_modes: Insufficient per-sample EV yield or per-vesicle cargo abundance → assay sensitivity falls below limit of detection producing false negatives and irreproducible lot comparisons.

Spike-in tracer physicochemistry or surface markers differ from endogenous EVs → spike-in recovery does not reflect endogenous EV recovery, producing false assay-validation signals or false confidence in negative results.
Capture antibody bias or inefficient capture of relevant EV subpopulations → selective sampling of non-representative subpopulations yields misleading fingerprints not generalizable across lots.

Incomplete protection assays (RNase/protease conditions not fully degrading external complexes) → retention of signal in 'protected' condition that actually arises from tightly bound non-vesicular complexes, causing false-positive attribution to intra-vesicular cargo.
Cross-reactivity or background in droplet assays (index-hopping, barcode collision, or ambient RNA/protein) → artifactual co-occurrence calls at the single-vesicle level confounding interpretation.

Low-input proteomics/lipidomics stochasticity → inability to reproducibly detect detergent-sensitive luminal proteins or consistent lipid-class context across lots, making composite fingerprint unmeasurable.

Secretome co-isolates that survive detergent/protease (e.g., lipoproteins, protein aggregates) → protected bulk signals persist and single-vesicle splits cannot disambiguate their contribution if separation and protease accessibility differ from assumptions.

Resource and method-development constraints → inability to fully optimize and orthogonally validate multiple novel single-vesicle readouts before material is exhausted, producing inconclusive experiments.
strongest_objection: The experiment can be invalidated by analytic insensitivity and mismatched spike-in behavior: if capture-positive fractions contain too few intact vesicles or too-low copy numbers of targeted protected small RNAs/proteins per vesicle, the droplet single-vesicle and low-input proteomic/lipidomic workflows may produce reproducible false negatives (or highly stochastic detection), and an exogenous spike-in tracer that does not mimic endogenous EV capture/recovery/protection will fail to validate assay performance—leaving positive bulk protected signals uninterpretable and preventing discrimination between bona fide intra-vesicular cargo and co-isolated, protection-resistant soluble complexes.
